Supporting DTW_ECG Reproducibility¶

DTW analysis and figures, No additional analyses are introduced.¶

This program compares a synthetically generated signal and a real ECG signal for academic demonstration only. Not for clinical use.¶

Load reference data¶

ECG wave from Physionet (ath_016 snap from 850 to 2000 record) need (ath_016.hea, ath_016.dat files)¶
SSingstad BJ. PhysioNet. 2022 [cited 2025 Mar 17]. Norwegian Endurance Athlete ECG Database v1.0.0. Available from: https://www.physionet.org/content/norwegian-athlete-ecg/1.0.0/¶
In [2]:
import wfdb
from scipy.signal import butter, filtfilt

# 1. Read the record
# Note: 'record_name' should not include the extension (.hea or .dat) in the same jupyter nottebook folder
record = wfdb.rdrecord('ath_016', sampfrom=850, sampto=2000, channels=[0, 1, 2])

# 2. Extract the physical signal (the mV values)
raw_data = record.p_signal
ecg_data_b = raw_data[280:640] #sellect a single ECG wave

# 3. remove the zero offsets if exist
### The ECG isoelectric line provides a zero-level reference that improves waveform comparison.
ecg_data_b[:, 0] = ecg_data_b[:, 0]+0.02
ecg_data_b[:, 1] = ecg_data_b[:, 1]+0.42
ecg_data_b[:, 2] = ecg_data_b[:, 2]+0.33

# 4. Filter the data
sampling_rate = 500 #sampling_rate = 500.0  # Assume a sample rate of 1Hz, modify as needed
num_samples = 300
cutoff_frequency = 60  # Adjust as needed for desired cutoff frequency
order = 4
scale_factor = sampling_rate
b, a = butter(order, cutoff_frequency, btype='low', fs=sampling_rate)
filt_ref_data = filtfilt(b, a, ecg_data_b[:], axis=0)  # Apply for denoising and improve the shape of the P signal

# 5. test loaded data
plt.figure(figsize=(7,2))
plt.plot(filt_ref_data[:, 0], linewidth=2)
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
plt.show()

# 6. Check the shape to confirm
print(f"Data shape: {filt_ref_data.shape}")
print(f"Data type: {filt_ref_data.dtype}")
print("The reference data and the simulated data must match in dimensionality.")

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from scipy import signal
from scipy.spatial.distance import cdist

# 1. Data Selection
# Assuming lead index 1 (Lead II) for both
s1 = filt_ref_data[:, 0]  # Reference (Database)
s2 = sym_data[:, 0]       # User Generated

# 2. Calculate Local Distance Matrix (Euclidean)
# Compares every point in s1 with every point in s2
cost_matrix = cdist(s1.reshape(-1, 1), s2.reshape(-1, 1), metric='euclidean')

# 3. Compute Accumulated Cost Matrix
# This is the core DTW logic to find the path of least resistance
acc_cost_matrix = np.zeros(cost_matrix.shape)
acc_cost_matrix[0, 0] = cost_matrix[0, 0]

# Initialize first row and column
for i in range(1, cost_matrix.shape[0]):
    acc_cost_matrix[i, 0] = cost_matrix[i, 0] + acc_cost_matrix[i-1, 0]
for j in range(1, cost_matrix.shape[1]):
    acc_cost_matrix[0, j] = cost_matrix[0, j] + acc_cost_matrix[0, j-1]

# Fill the matrix using the recursive rule
for i in range(1, cost_matrix.shape[0]):
    for j in range(1, cost_matrix.shape[1]):
        acc_cost_matrix[i, j] = cost_matrix[i, j] + np.min([
            acc_cost_matrix[i-1, j],    # Insertion
            acc_cost_matrix[i, j-1],    # Deletion
            acc_cost_matrix[i-1, j-1]   # Match
        ])

# 4. Backtracking: Find the Optimal Warping Path
path = []
i, j = acc_cost_matrix.shape[0] - 1, acc_cost_matrix.shape[1] - 1
path.append((i, j))

while i > 0 or j > 0:
    options = []
    if i > 0: options.append((acc_cost_matrix[i-1, j], (i-1, j)))
    if j > 0: options.append((acc_cost_matrix[i, j-1], (i, j-1)))
    if i > 0 and j > 0: options.append((acc_cost_matrix[i-1, j-1], (i-1, j-1)))

    # Choose the neighbor with the lowest accumulated cost
    min_val, (i, j) = min(options, key=lambda x: x[0])
    path.append((i, j))

path = np.array(path[::-1]) # Reverse to start from (0,0)

# 5. Statistical Similarity Metrics
# Calculate Cross-Correlation to find natural shift
correlation = signal.correlate(s1 - np.mean(s1), s2 - np.mean(s2), mode='full')
lags = signal.correlation_lags(len(s1), len(s2), mode='full')
found_lag = lags[np.argmax(correlation)]

# Calculate Similarity Percentage (Pearson Correlation) at Lag 0
similarity_pct = np.corrcoef(s1, s2)[0, 1] * 100

# Calculate DTW Metrics
dtw_distance = acc_cost_matrix[-1, -1]
norm_dtw = dtw_distance / (len(s1) + len(s2))

# --- Visualization ---
# --- Global font Settings ---
plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.size': 18,           # Base font size
    'axes.titlesize': 18,      # Subplot titles
    'axes.labelsize': 18,      # X and Y labels
    'xtick.labelsize': 14,     # X-axis tick numbers
    'ytick.labelsize': 14,     # Y-axis tick numbers
    'legend.fontsize': 14,     # Legend text
    'figure.titlesize': 24     # Main figure title
})

%config InlineBackend.figure_format = 'retina'
plt.figure(figsize=(17, 5))

# Plot A: Raw Signals
plt.subplot(1, 3, 1)
plt.plot(s1, label='Database (Ref)', color='blue', linewidth=1.5)
plt.plot(s2, label='User (Query)', color='black', linewidth=1.5, alpha=0.8)
plt.title("a. Raw Signals (Natural State)")
plt.xlabel("Samples")
plt.ylabel("Amplitude (mV)")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(alpha=0.2)

# Plot B: Alignment
plt.subplot(1, 3, 2)
for (map_x, map_y) in path[::15]: # Sample every 15 for visual clarity
    plt.plot([map_x, map_y], [s1[map_x], s2[map_y] + 1.5], color='gray', alpha=0.3)
plt.plot(s1, label='Database', color='blue')
plt.plot(s2 + 1.5, label='User (+1.5)', color='black')
plt.title("b. Dynamic Time Warping Alignment")
plt.xlabel("Samples")
plt.legend(loc='lower right')

# Plot C: Cost Matrix & Summary
plt.subplot(1, 3, 3)
plt.imshow(acc_cost_matrix.T, origin='lower', cmap='viridis', aspect='auto')
plt.plot(path[:, 0], path[:, 1], 'w-', linewidth=2, label='Optimal Path')
plt.title(f"c. Accumulated Cost\nSimilarity: {similarity_pct:.2f}% | Norm DTW: {norm_dtw:.4f}")
plt.colorbar(label='Cost Value')
plt.xlabel('Database Index')
plt.ylabel('User Index')

plt.tight_layout()
#plt.savefig('ecg_similarity.svg', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight') #This save an image of the plot 
plt.show()

print(f"Summary Report:")
print(f"----------------")
print(f"Pearson Similarity: {similarity_pct:.2f}%")
print(f"Natural Lag:        {found_lag} samples")
print(f"Normalized DTW:     {norm_dtw:.4f}")

Original Vs Warped Alignment and Similarity¶

This ensures the correlation measures morphology (the shape of the wave) rather than just timing, since the ECG signals often have slight phase shifts in the timing of the P, QRS, and T waves.¶
(V. Tuzcu and S. Nas, 'Dynamic time warping as a novel tool in pattern recognition of ECG changes in heart rhythm disturbances,' 2005 IEEE International Conference on Systems, Man and Cybernetics, Waikoloa, HI, USA, 2005, pp. 182-186 Vol. 1, doi: 10.1109/ICSMC.2005.1571142.¶
In [4]:
%config InlineBackend.figure_format = 'retina'
from fastdtw import fastdtw
from scipy.stats import pearsonr
from matplotlib.ticker import MultipleLocator, FuncFormatter

threshold = 0.9  # Similarity threshold, a warped correlation > 0.85 is typically considered a "high fidelity"

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.size': 14,           # Base font size
    'axes.titlesize': 14,      # Subplot titles
    'axes.labelsize': 10,      # X and Y labels
    'xtick.labelsize': 8,     # X-axis tick numbers
    'ytick.labelsize': 8,     # Y-axis tick numbers
    'legend.fontsize': 8,     # Legend text
    'figure.titlesize': 12     # Main figure title
})

fig, axs = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(10, 7), sharex=True, sharey=True)
summary_data = []

leads = ['Lead I', 'Lead II', 'Lead III']
colors = ['teal', 'darkorange', 'crimson']

for i in range(3):
    # 1. Plot - Side-by-Side Comparison
    # --- Column 0: Synthetic Data (symu_data) ---
    axs[i, 0].plot(sym_data[:, i], label='Synthetic Data', color=colors[i], linewidth=1)
    axs[i, 0].plot(filt_ref_data[:, i], label='Real Data', color='black', linewidth=1)
    axs[i, 0].set_ylabel(f'{leads[i]}\n(mV)')
    axs[i, 0].grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
    axs[i, 0].legend(loc='lower right')

    # 2. Prepare data
    ref = filt_ref_data[:, i]
    query = sym_data[:, i]

    # 3. Compute DTW Alignment
    distance, path = fastdtw(ref, query, dist=lambda x, y: np.abs(x - y))
    
    # 4. "Warp" the signals using the path to align them in time
    ref_aligned = np.array([ref[p[0]] for p in path])
    query_aligned = np.array([query[p[1]] for p in path])
    
    # 5. Calculate Warped Correlation
    #Pearson correlation is inherently invariant to amplitude scaling.
    correlation, _ = pearsonr(ref_aligned, query_aligned)
    
    is_correlated = "Yes" if correlation >= threshold else "No"
    summary_data.append([leads[i], distance, correlation, is_correlated])
    
    # 6. Plotting
    # We plot against a generic index because the path changes the 'time' scale
    axs[i, 1].plot(ref_aligned, label=f'Real {leads[i]} (Aligned)', color='black', alpha=0.5)
    axs[i, 1].plot(query_aligned, label=f'Sym {leads[i]} (Aligned)', color=colors[i], linestyle='--')
    
    axs[i, 1].set_title(f"{leads[i]}: Warped Correlation = {correlation:.3f} ({is_correlated})")


    
    axs[i, 0].xaxis.set_major_locator(MultipleLocator(100))  # Major ticks every 100 points
    axs[i, 0].xaxis.set_minor_locator(MultipleLocator(20))   # Minor ticks every 20 points
    axs[i, 0].yaxis.set_major_locator(MultipleLocator(0.6))  # Major ticks every 5 units
    axs[i, 0].yaxis.set_minor_locator(MultipleLocator(0.15))  # Minor ticks every 1 unit

    axs[i, 0].grid(which='major', color='black', linestyle='--')
    axs[i, 0].grid(which='minor', color='#CCCCCC', linestyle=':')
    axs[i, 0].grid(True, which='both')   
    

    axs[i, 1].legend(loc='lower right')
    #axs[i, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
    
# Set titles for the columns
axs[0, 0].set_title('Original Signals')
#axs[0, 1].set_title('Real Filtered Signal', fontweight='bold')

# Set shared X-axis label
axs[2, 0].set_xlabel('Samples')
axs[2, 1].set_xlabel('Elastic time shifting, to compare P, QRS and T waves')

plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
plt.savefig('ecg_plot_three_leads.svg', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# 7. --- Print Final Analysis ---
print(f"{'Lead':<10} | {'DTW Dist':<12} | {'Warped Corr':<12} | {'Status'}")
print("-" * 55)
correlated_count = 0
for row in summary_data:
    print(f"{row[0]:<10} | {row[1]:<12.2f} | {row[2]:<12.4f} | {row[3]}")
    if row[3] == "Yes":
        correlated_count += 1

print(f"\nResult: {correlated_count} out of 3 leads are highly correlated.")

fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4.5), sharex=True, sharey=True)
summary_data = []

leads = ['Lead I', 'Lead II', 'Lead III']
colors = ['teal', 'darkorange', 'crimson']

for i in range(3):

    # 2. Prepare data
    ref = filt_ref_data[:, i]
    query = sym_data[:, i]
    # 3. Compute DTW Alignment
    distance, path = fastdtw(ref, query, dist=lambda x, y: np.abs(x - y))
    
    # 4. "Warp" the signals using the path to align them in time
    ref_aligned = np.array([ref[p[0]] for p in path])
    query_aligned = np.array([query[p[1]] for p in path])

    # Assuming you already ran: distance, path = fastdtw(ref_lead, made_lead)
    # Extract the path indices
    path_x = [p[0] for p in path]
    path_y = [p[1] for p in path]

    # 1. Plot the Warping Path
    axs[i].plot(path_x, path_y, color='blue', linewidth=2, label='Warping Path')

    # 2. Plot a Reference Diagonal (Perfect match line)
    axs[i].plot([0, 320], [0, 320], color='red', linestyle='--', alpha=0.5, label='Ideal Diagonal')

    # Labeling for your paper
    axs[i].set_title(f"{leads[i]}")
    axs[i].legend(loc='lower right')
    #axs[i].set_title("DTW Warping Path: Natural vs. Synthetic ECG")
    axs[i].set_xlabel("Reference Signal Index (PhysioNet)")

    axs[i].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
    axs[i].legend()
axs[0].set_ylabel("Synthetic Signal Index")
